title: The mermaid boundary test fails about half its runs on the forge and none locally
foundBy: session agent, while dispatching ci on a branch before merging it

evidence.verified: Five `ci` dispatches on `current-ui-work` at afff93a all reported `completed success`. The two `check` legs carry this test, so that is 10 of 10 legs green, and none of them needed a re-run. Before the change the test failed 3 of 6 observed legs, including both legs of one push to `main`. If that rate had held, five clean runs would occur about 3 percent of the time. Removing the diagram from the test still fails it, 13 seconds in, so the larger budget does not mask a real failure. `npm run ci` exits 0 at afff93a.

details:
`src/components/MarkdownViewer.mermaid.test.tsx` fails intermittently on the forge and has never been seen failing locally. The test is `renders a diagram without interpreting markdown-authored HTML labels`. It fails with `AssertionError: expected null not to be null`, and the DOM it prints carries `data-mermaid-rendered="false"`. The diagram has not finished rendering when the assertion runs.

Six observations on 2026-09-09, all on the same unchanged tree at f9a9f65. Run 34297095690, a dispatch on the branch, failed the node 22.13 leg and passed node 24. Run 34299539699, the push to `main`, failed both legs. Re-running the failed jobs in each turned every leg green. That is three failures and three passes of one test on identical code.

It is not a node version quirk, because it failed on both legs at once. It is not this branch, because the five commits it landed with touch nothing under `src/` and no test or config file. `npm run check` and `npm run ci` ran green many times locally across 2026-09-08.

Two things make this worse than a slow test. The `npm` workflow runs its own `npm run check` and does not wait for `ci`, so on that push the same commit failed the test in one workflow and passed it in the other, and the publishing one won. A version reached the dev channel while `ci` was red.

The second is that re-running rewrites the record. `gh run list` now reports both of those runs as `success`, because a re-run replaces the conclusion. The failures are visible only in this record and in job logs that age out.

notes.text:
The failure was never reproduced locally. The fix rests on a margin measurement rather than on watching the test fail.

Twenty attempts across one, two and four core sandboxes all passed, with a cold Vite cache, the full suite running and every core busy. Fewer cores ran the test faster rather than slower, because vitest parallelises less and nothing then competes with the import. Core count is not the lever, and what the forge does differently is unmeasured.

What is measured is the margin. The wait covers a dynamic import of the Mermaid library and a render, and it took 580 to 647 milliseconds of testing-library's 1000 millisecond default in the slowest local configuration. No other test loads the real library, which is why no other test shows this.

The clean dispatches settle one open question. A larger budget helps a slow render and does nothing for a hung one, so the failure was slowness.
